miss_rate.value: 14/94 = 14.9% (blind audit R3, verified); 19.2% counting five boundary makers ruled into other verticals; up to 26/106 = 24.5% if the 12 unverified candidates are real
miss_rate.note: Third blind audit (two auditors, new methods, 2026-11-17) after closure pass 5 (OSHA 300A establishments in NAICS 333120, 333131, 333922, 332313, each verified by a sourced in-definition product at the site). Miss rate = verified misses / (included plants found + verified misses), as in R2; excluded plants found leave the count; plants in the ledger under another city or name count as found after verification. R3-C: 4 misses of 46; R3-D: 10 of 67; combined unique 14 of 94. All verified misses are now base records; merging them does not lower the measured rate.
history: 14.9% verified (Nov 17, blind audit R3 after the OSHA closure)

known_limits: Miss rate: the third blind audit (R3, two auditors with new methods: state directories and product search; dealer line cards, buyer's guides, supplier awards, trademarks, news) found 14 verified misses among 94 in-definition plants (14.9%); 19.2% if the five lifting- and tractor-led attachment makers ruled into other verticals were counted; 24.5% if all 12 unverifiable leads were real. Neither auditor reached a dry point (both stopped at their search budgets). Misses were small attachment makers (compact, excavator) and small underground-mining and aggregate shops.

16 OSHA-closure base records and 7 verified misses have prospect_test unknown (manufacturing of an in-definition product at the site is stated, welding is not); they are held as base, not profiled (Caterpillar Clayton precedent).

The two verified misses that ranked in the top 40 with counted postings were profiled afterwards: Fecon, Lebanon OH, 76 High (three undated welder postings open at once; boundary, forestry mulching attachments) and General Steel & Supply (Fisher Industries), Dickinson ND, 28 Low under the strict campus rule (75 High if a 2021 source placing both fabrication facilities on its Energy Drive campus is accepted). The top 40 is now fully profiled.

About 155 EPA registry rows and named leads from closure remain unverified, plus 15 re-audit candidates and leads such as Tricon's other plants, Power Curbers' Cedar Falls and McHenry plants, HitchDoc's Kwik-Way Sioux Falls plant and Amerequip's New Holstein plants. The R3 closure (OSHA 300A NAICS 333120, 333131, 333922, 332313) screened 776 establishments: 37 base records added, 2 excluded, the rest triaged out or already present; 42 remain unverified leads.

Fact-check: round 1 11.4%; round 2 (all 47 profiles, rotated) 3.3%; round 3 (the 21 newest profiles) 16/417 = 3.8% overall, but 7.3% for profiler I's seven (12.8% counting untrimmed sibling rows). All corrections applied. The round-3 sweep of compound-value clauses was run only on the newest profiles. A separate sample of 25 closure base records found 1.5%.

Brookville Equipment, Brookville PA scores 63 Medium under the written campus rule: the flat car's size is a company-level fact and a second Brookville site (service and rebuilds) is 1.3 km away. If the rebuild shop is ruled not a production site, it is 83 High.

Material scores 0 on 59 of 68 profiled plants: mining and construction sources rarely state a welded part's size or weight, and payloads, bucket capacities and machine classes do not count as part sizes.

Paladin Dexter MI is profiled as a boundary plant: no Paladin page says what it builds, and EPA's facility name (Sweepster-Harley Attachments) points to sweeper and broom attachments, which would exclude it under the M-B New Holstein ruling.
Auditor B could see file names (not contents) in the shared scratchpad during the re-audit, so its blindness is slightly weaker than auditor A's.

Opening lines and bottleneck guesses of all 71 profiled plants were rebuilt under constrained composition (each clause from one stated row with its date; postings 'listed'; no live counts) and gated by tools/validate_lines.py; the round-6 line check found 2/134 = 1.5% (1/100 on High and Medium). Three lines rested on postings that closed on 2026-11-17 and were replaced; the closures moved labor at Rockland Bedford (73 -> 65), Virnig Rice (58 -> 46); Mellott Warfordsburg's posting was re-read as a batch re-list standing ad (60 -> 52); Kafka Mosinee's careers-page ad has no apply flow of its own (55 -> 43).
The company-level sweep (round 7, targeted: 64 flagged rows) retagged 41 stated rows as inferred (company or two-site pages tagged stated at one plant); no score or confidence moved.

Cross-vertical checks (round 8: Standard Iron's entrant profile, permits, OSHA) are 12.1%, mostly Standard Iron's brand-level rows, now retagged; Standard Iron Sumner is 26 Low and Innovation Way is held as base because their welder posting names both Hartford plants.
Profiled: 71 plants; the rest of the included plants are base records with no score.
